global.title: Rescuing astronomy from its satellite megaconstellation crisis
global.summary: In the late 1800s, long enough ago that it’s almost been forgotten, research astronomy faced an existential crisis brought on by the lighting of cities in the early industrial age. Such electric lighting created strong sky brightness (now called light pollution), which forced research-grade astronomical observatories to move from cities to remote, “dark sky” sites. global.title: How mini-constellations could more quickly bring new tech to Europe, and to orbit
global.summary: When the European thermal-imagery company constellr began working with Space Inventor on its next generation of satellites, some of the most important details of the spacecraft had yet to be finalized.
